📋 Platform Rules: Dos & Don'ts · Lesson 7 of 7

WhatsApp Business: The Dos, Don'ts & Number-Ban Mistakes

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

A Kenyan lender was ordered to pay KES 400,000 to one man for sending him loan promos by SMS and phone that he'd never agreed to. Your WhatsApp broadcasts fall under the same Data Protection Act.

In that case (ODPC Complaint No. 1951 of 2024, against Platinum Credit), the man had never given the company his data or his consent. Now picture a salon blasting offers to 600 numbers copied out of a chama group. WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy says the same thing: only message people who gave you their number and agreed to hear from you, and respect every request to stop. Break it and WhatsApp can limit or remove your access, and for terminated accounts it can bar your business for good.

6.8M
WhatsApp accounts banned in the first half of 2025 for links to organised scam centres (Meta, via The Daily Star)
DODON'T
Message customers who gave you their number and said yesBuy number lists or copy members out of groups
End promos with 'Reply STOP to opt out', and honour every STOPKeep messaging people who asked you to stop
Use the official WhatsApp Business appUse GB WhatsApp, WhatsApp Plus or other modded apps
Use broadcast lists (they only reach people who saved your number)Use bulk-sender or auto-messaging tools on a normal number
Ask before adding anyone to a groupAdd strangers to groups. WhatsApp now shows them a safety notice and an easy exit
List clothes, food, beauty services and handmade goods in your catalogueList alcohol, vapes, live animals, prescription drugs, betting or shared Netflix/Showmax logins in the catalogue
Confirm payment in your own M-Pesa message or appRelease goods because someone sent a 'confirmation' screenshot
Turn on two-step verification (a 6-digit PIN)Share your registration code with anyone, even 'Safaricom'
Use your real business name and photoName your profile 'M-Pesa Support' or copy a brand's logo
Keep messages useful and occasionalSend five promos a day until people block you

What gets numbers restricted or banned

  • Being blocked or reported by lots of people in a short time. Blocks and reports hurt a business's quality rating, and when quality stays low WhatsApp rate-limits the business.
  • Bulk or automated messaging at a speed no human could manage.
  • Unofficial apps. WhatsApp has temporarily banned users of mods like GB WhatsApp and told them to switch to the official app.
  • Selling prohibited items. WhatsApp's Commerce Policy (which follows Meta's Commerce Policy) bans categories including alcohol, tobacco, animals, real-money gambling, adult products, weapons, and digital subscriptions or accounts.

The risk ladder: no likes to remove, so it starts higher

  1. Quality drop and rate limits. Fewer messages get delivered.
  2. Temporary ban. Common with modded apps and mass messaging.
  3. Permanent ban. You lose the number on WhatsApp, and with it your chats, catalogue and customer list. Warnings aren't guaranteed.
📋 Opt-in message (send once, keep the replies)
Hi [Name]! 👋 This is [Business] in [Area]. We send new stock and offers on WhatsApp about once a week.
Would you like to receive them? Reply YES to join.
You can reply STOP any time and we'll remove you. Asante!

Kenyan specifics

  • Consent is law, not courtesy. Under the Data Protection Act, marketing needs consent. The Platinum Credit case shows one complaint can cost hundreds of thousands of shillings.
  • Fake job tasks. The DCI has warned about unsolicited WhatsApp 'work from home' offers that later ask you to download an app to get paid. The app can be malware. Block those numbers.
  • No betting promos on Status. BCLB's May 2025 rules ban creators from promoting gambling on any platform, and your Status counts.
✗ MYTH

A broadcast list is private, so consent doesn't matter.

✓ REALITY

Private delivery doesn't change the law or WhatsApp's policy. Both require opt-in. Broadcasts also only reach people who saved your number, which is why saving your number is the cleanest proof that someone wants to hear from you.

✅ Your 10-minute rules audit
⚡ Quick check

Which of these is banned from your WhatsApp Business catalogue under the Commerce Policy?

WhatsApp's Commerce Policy prohibits selling digital content, subscriptions and accounts. Reselling streaming logins is a popular side hustle, and it can get a business number restricted.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Only message people who agreed to hear from you. That's WhatsApp policy and Kenyan law.
  2. Blocks, reports, mods and bulk tools are the fastest ways to lose a number.
  3. Check your catalogue against the Commerce Policy. Alcohol, animals and digital subscriptions are out.
  4. WhatsApp bans can be permanent and come without warning, so back up your customer list.
